analysis.title: The AI reset – Fundamentals take centre stage
key_insights: The recent global tech sell-off reflects greater scrutiny of valuations and of whether rising AI investment is turning into earnings. It does not signal a breakdown of the AI growth story.
Investors are focusing on AI capital expenditure, free cash flow and investment returns rather than AI-related revenue growth alone.
The latest earnings season shows AI demand has not weakened. Cloud growth rates were Microsoft Azure +48% y/y, Amazon AWS +39% y/y and Alphabet Google Cloud +103% y/y.

Microsoft delivered 19% overall revenue growth alongside Azure's strength and kept free cash flow positive. Alphabet's advertising revenue came in below market expectations and its free cash flow turned negative despite strong Google Cloud growth.
Intel's Data Center and AI revenue grew 78% y/y on AI server and Xeon CPU demand. Client Computing revenue fell 5% and Foundry remained loss-making.
Eastspring Taiwan PM Eric Lin sees the market moving from a broad AI thematic re-rating toward a phase that rewards fundamentals, earnings delivery and returns on AI investment.

AI applications are broadening from model training to inference and Agentic AI. PM Jack Hsu remains positive on AI computing infrastructure, memory, high-speed networking and optical components, and semiconductor equipment.
HBM, advanced packaging and high-end substrates demand remains strong. Thermal management, power management, PCBs and copper-clad laminates benefit from AI server specification upgrades.
The team expects performance to become more differentiated, favoring companies with tangible AI revenue contribution, earnings growth and reasonable valuations.
The team is using the correction to add selected AI supply-chain names in memory, ABF substrates, semiconductor equipment and passive components.

sector_views.rationale: Long-term AI demand is intact and the beneficiary set is broadening from GPUs into CPUs, memory, networking, packaging, substrates, power and thermal. The team prefers names with strong earnings growth and reasonable valuations.

earnings_insights: Microsoft Azure revenue +48% y/y and total revenue +19% y/y, with positive free cash flow (latest reported quarter).
Amazon AWS revenue +39% y/y (latest reported quarter).
Alphabet Google Cloud revenue +103% y/y. Advertising revenue came in below market expectations and free cash flow turned negative (latest reported quarter).
Intel Data Center and AI revenue +78% y/y, Client Computing revenue -5% y/y, Foundry still loss-making (latest reported quarter).
risk_factors: Rising AI capital expenditure with negative free cash flow, as at Alphabet, could make investors more cautious about near-term returns.
Elevated tech valuations remain exposed to further scrutiny.
Weakness in non-AI business lines, such as Intel's Client Computing and Foundry, can offset AI growth.
vol_and_positioning: Global technology stocks saw another significant correction last week. The report attributes it to valuation adjustment and scrutiny of AI capex, free cash flow and returns, not weaker AI demand.

tension_points.bull_case: AI demand is growing rapidly, with cloud revenue up 39% to 103% y/y, and infrastructure spending is broadening across memory, networking, packaging and substrates.
tension_points.bear_case: Investors question whether rising AI capex turns into broader revenue, earnings and free cash flow. Alphabet's ad revenue missed and its free cash flow turned negative.

theme_stances.key_argument: The correction reflects valuation and returns scrutiny, not weaker AI demand, and the long-term AI growth outlook is unchanged.
theme_stances.evidence: recent correction has not changed the structural long-term growth outlook for AI

theme_stances.key_argument: Investment is expanding beyond GPUs into CPUs, memory, networking, packaging, substrates, power and thermal, which widens the range of beneficiaries.
theme_stances.evidence: range of beneficiaries across the AI supply chain is likely to continue to broaden
